simplebuildingtools.blueprint.help.copy_: Copies the whole guide to the clipboard - for example to ask an AI to write a blueprint for you.
simplebuildingtools.blueprint.help.guide: A blueprint describes a building as text: every line places blocks, and the preview shows the result while you type. Sign it, hold it in your off hand and a building wand in your main hand, and a click builds it with the blocks from your inventory.
Blocks tab (opens first): type a name or ID into the field, pick a block from the list and press Insert - or press Enter, or double-click it. Its ID goes into the code at the cursor.

Shapes instead of positions: sphere(8,8,8,5) (center, radius), dome(8,0,8,5), cylinder(4,0,4,3,6) and pyramid(4,0,4,3,4) (base center, radius, height), box(0,0,0,5,4,5) (corner, size), line(0,0,0..9,4,2). Given a box instead, e.g. sphere(0..9,0..5,0..9), they fill the same figure as an octant.
hollow_ in front keeps only the shell: hollow_sphere(8,8,8,5), hollow_box(0,0,0,5,4,5). Shapes repeat like positions: stone sphere(2,2,2,1)*3@5,0,0.

Variables: $r = 5, then $r works in positions, sizes and repeat counts, with + - * / % and brackets: $h = $r * 2 + 1, stone 0..$r,0,$h-1. In a position write multiplication in brackets, ($r*2), because * starts a repetition.
Preview: drag to rotate, Ctrl + drag to move, mouse wheel to zoom; the round arrow in its corner resets the view.
Mistakes are underlined in red and explained below the code; the line under it counts the characters (at most 32000). Your work saves itself while you type.
Materials lists what the building costs; below it are the size, the block count and the smallest building wand that can build it, with a bar up to that wand's limit.
Sign gives the blueprint a title and locks it - only signed blueprints build. A blueprint laid down with sneak + right-click opens again with a right-click of an empty hand.
Copy text below copies this whole guide - paste it into a chat with an AI and ask it to write a blueprint for you.

A line is a block name followed by a position: stone 0,0,0 places one stone. A position is x,y,z - x runs east, y up, z south, each from 0 to 255. Several positions may follow on one line, separated by spaces. # starts a comment.
Ranges fill many blocks at once: a..b on any axis, both ends included. stone 0..4,0,0..4 is a 5 x 1 x 5 floor. The corner form stone 1,1,1..1,1,5 fills from one corner to the other.
Block names are IDs like oak_planks or glass - the Blocks tab shows the ID of every block. minecraft: may be left out; blocks of other mods need their prefix.
Properties go in brackets: oak_stairs[facing=east,half=top] 0,3,0. Properties you leave out keep the block's default.
Repeat: oak_fence 0,1,0*5@2,0,0 places 5 copies, each 2 blocks further along x. The offset may be negative.
air clears what earlier lines placed: air 1..3,1..3,1..3 hollows out a box.
Alias: $roof = oak_stairs[facing=north] gives a block a short name; then write $roof 0..4,4,0.
Later lines overwrite earlier ones at the same spot, so write the big parts first and the details after.

text.autoconfig.simplebuildingtools.opti:
Off: blueprints neither open their editor nor
build with the Building Wand. Its recipes
vanish with the next /reload or world start.
Server-side, sent to clients. Default: on.

At most this many positions a blueprint build
places per tick; lower values make big builds
take longer and spare the server. 1 to 32768
(the default is above anything a build uses
today). Server-side. Default: 32768.

Accept build code with pixels rows made
from a picture (Import > Picture...). Off
refuses such code when it is saved.
Server-side. Default: on.

Longest edge of a picture blueprint in
blocks, 16 to 128. Server-side.
Default: 128.

Operator level a player needs for picture
blueprints: 0 everyone, 2 game masters,
4 owners only. Server-side. Default: 0.

Experimental. Building a lot at once makes
you hungry: per click or blueprint build the
first blocks are free (1/16 of the wand's
largest cube, at least 256 - normal faces
never cost anything); every block past that
adds food exhaustion, less for stronger wands
(a Copper Wand filling 16x16x16 takes about a
quarter of the hunger bar, an Enderite Wand
building 128x128x128 the whole bar). Creative
mode is exempt. It never deals damage itself.
Server-side. Default: on.

Server-side. 0 to 10.
Multiplies the food exhaustion of every block
past the free allowance (see Building Wand
Hunger Cost). 0.5 = half as hungry, 2 = twice
as hungry, 0 = building is free. The free
allowance itself stays. Server-side. Default:
1.0.
